name: european-dates
title: Day-first dates
prompt:
The app is used in Algeria and France, where dates are written day/month/year (e.g. `25/12/2026`).
In `dates.py`, `parse_date` fails or swaps day and month, and `format_date` prints the month first.

Fix both:
- `parse_date` accepts `25/12/2026`, `25-12-2026` and `25.12.2026`, single-digit day/month
  (`1/2/2026` is 1 February), and ignores surrounding spaces. It returns a `datetime.date`.
- Invalid dates (e.g. `31/02/2026`, `hello`) raise `ValueError`.
- `format_date` returns `DD/MM/YYYY` with zero padding.
